biological.citation: SATB2 preserves colon stem cell identity and mediates ileum-colon conversion via enhancer remodeling (PMID: 34582804)
biological.summary: SATB2 is a colon-restricted chromatin factor that singularly preserves LGR5+ adult colonic stem cell and epithelial identity. Satb2 loss in adult mice leads to stable conversion of colonic stem cells into ileal-like stem cells and replacement of colonic mucosa with ileum-like tissue. SATB2 regulates colonic identity by modulating enhancer binding of CDX2 and HNF4A transcription factors.

biological.citation: Astrocyte layers in the mammalian cerebral cortex revealed by a single-cell in situ transcriptomic map (PMID: 32203496)
biological.summary: Satb2 expression was identified as a marker distinguishing neuronal layer identity in the mouse cortex. Satb2 mutations that shifted neuronal post-mitotic development were sufficient to alter glial layering, indicating an instructive role for neuronal cues in organizing astrocyte layers.

biological.citation: ARID1B controls transcriptional programs of axon projection in an organoid model of the human corpus callosum (PMID: 38718796)
biological.summary: Neurons expressing SATB2, a determinant of callosal projection neuron (CPN) identity, show impaired maturation in ARID1B+/- neural organoids. SATB2+ neurons display reduced chromatin accessibility in regions targeted by TCF-like, NFI-like, and ARID-like transcription factors, impairing long-range axonal projections.

biological.citation: A critical period of translational control during brain development at codon resolution (PMID: 36482253)
biological.summary: Timed translation upregulation of Satb2, a chromatin-binding protein essential for neuronal subtype differentiation, restricts protein expression in neuronal lineages despite broad transcriptional priming in progenitors. Satb2 translation is dynamically regulated during mid-gestation neocortex neurogenesis.

biological.citation: SATB2 Mediates H3K9 Delactylation by Recruiting HDAC3 to Repress LCN2 and Inhibit Lung Tumor Growth and Metastasis (PMID: 41736683)
biological.summary: SATB2 functions as a negative regulator of global histone lactylation and tumor suppressor in NSCLC. SATB2 binds the LCN2 promoter and recruits HDAC3 via its N-terminal domain to catalyze H3K9 delactylation and repress LCN2 transcription. SATB2 overexpression inhibited xenograft tumor growth and lung metastasis.

biological.citation: Protein translation rate determines neocortical neuron fate (PMID: 38849354)
biological.summary: Ire1α regulates Satb2 expression and neuronal polarity as a post-transcriptional mechanism. Satb2 mRNA translation requires eIF4A1 helicase activity towards its 5'-untranslated region. Ire1α-safeguarded proteostasis serves as an essential regulator of Satb2 expression during brain development.

biological.citation: APOE4 impacts cortical neurodevelopment and alters network formation in human brain organoids (PMID: 39416105)
biological.summary: APOE4 decreased BRN2+ and SATB2+ cortical neurons in iPSC-derived cortical organoids, while increasing astrocytes and outer radial glia. SATB2+ neuron reduction was associated with increased cell death and dysregulated GABA-related gene expression.
biological.sample_size: iPSC-derived cortical and ganglionic eminence organoids

biological.citation: YAP-Activated SATB2 Is a Coactivator of NRF2 That Amplifies Antioxidative Capacity and Promotes Tumor Progression in Renal Cell Carcinoma (PMID: 36598364)
biological.summary: SATB2 is upregulated in RCC and acts as an oncogenic chromatin organizer. YAP/TEAD4 activates SATB2 expression. SATB2 coordinates with NRF2 to drive enhancer-promoter interactions and amplify transcriptional activity of antioxidative genes. SATB2 recruits SWI/SNF complex subunits (BRD7, BRG1) to sustain DNA accessibility.
biological.sample_size: RCC cell lines, patient-derived xenografts, and organoids

biological.citation: Multiomic profiling of transcription factor binding and function in human brain (PMID: 38831039)
biological.summary: SATB2 is a neuronal transcription factor that binds unique genomic regions depleted for high-occupancy sites and promotes neuronal gene expression. SATB2 binding sites are enriched for risk variants associated with neuropsychiatric disorders, predominantly in neurons.
biological.sample_size: postmortem brain regions from multiple individuals

biological.citation: SATB2 organizes the 3D genome architecture of cognition in cortical neurons (PMID: 38244545)
biological.summary: SATB2 is genetically linked to human intelligence and acts as a cell-type-specific 3D genome modulator. SATB2 affects chromatin looping between enhancers and promoters of neuronal-activity-regulated genes, alters A/B compartments and topologically associating domains. SATB2 operates both independently and cooperatively with CTCF to set up the chromatin landscape for cognitive processes.
